title: 3D Mathematical Shapes & Trajectory Ribbon Tracers Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/MATH_SHAPE_3D_AND_TRACE_PATH_ARCHITECTURE.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/MATH_SHAPE_3D_AND_TRACE_PATH_ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/MATH_SHAPE_3D_AND_TRACE_PATH_ARCHITECTURE.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Pedagogical mathematical animation requires visual idioms distinct from conventional video game 3D graphics:

items: **[`MathShape3D`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/composites/geometry/MathShape3D.ts)**: Implements the iconic 3Blue1Brown / Manim mathematical aesthetic: semi-translucent volumetric surface bodies with glass transmission/refraction, paired with crisp 3D extruded stroke outlines along all unique geometric edges.

**[`TracePath`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/TracePath.ts)**: A real-time trajectory motion ribbon that dynamically follows moving entities or particles, smoothing anchor points via ping-pong GPU compute Chaikin subdivision and tapering dissipating tails.

children.description: Line3D unique edges; analytical joints and consistent width.

children: Evaluates lighting with an ambient floor, ensuring that back faces and shadowed regions remain saturated and mathematically readable without pitch-black falloff.
Extracts every unique topological edge in the mesh.
Renders each edge as an extruded 3D cylinder/ribbon ([`Line3D`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/3d/Line3D.ts)).

blocks.text: Given a triangle mesh with indices $[i_0, i_1, i_2]$:

items: Every triangle produces three candidate edges: $(i_0, i_1)$, $(i_1, i_2)$, $(i_2, i_0)$.
Edges are normalized so that $u = \min(i_a, i_b)$ and $v = \max(i_a, i_b)$.
Stored in a hash map `Map<string, [Vec3, Vec3]>` keyed by `${u}_${v}`. Shared interior edges between adjacent triangles are collapsed to a single edge, preventing overlapping duplicate line draws.

blocks.text: `TracePath` records historical spatial coordinates of a moving target:

blocks.code:
Head (t = scene.time)                           Tail (t - maxAge)
Full Stroke Width                               Tapered Width -> 0
Opacity: 1.0                                    Opacity: 0.0
   ●═════════════════════════════════════════════════┄┄

blocks.text: Rather than drawing rigid polygonal segments between discrete frame samples, `TracePath` executes GPU compute passes ([`chaikin_smooth.wgsl`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/shaders/compute/chaikin_smooth.wgsl)) using ping-pong storage buffers:

items: **Chaikin Corner-Cutting**: For segment $(\mathbf{P}_i, \mathbf{P}_{i+1})$, two new sub-points are generated:
Configurable iterations (`smoothing: 0..3`) produce silky ribbons even with erratic physics step updates.

blocks.text: B. Dynamic Age Dissipation & Inverted Anchoring

items: Points older than `maxAge` (default $1000\text{ms}$) are pruned from the tail.
Parameter $t=0$ corresponds to the **head** (newest point) and $t=1$ corresponds to the **tail** (oldest point).
Dash patterns and taper shaders support `anchorEnd: true`, measuring pattern distance from the moving head to prevent dashes from "swimming" across the ribbon as it grows.
